purpose: Two distinct things. tests/ (184 pytest tests + committed sha256-hashed "receipt" JSONs) validates the SupplyMind OpenEnv environment: graph/disruption/financial/reward engines, Pydantic contracts, task registry, FastAPI endpoints (reset/step/state/grader), OpenEnv spec compliance, grader discrimination/determinism, and an adversarial reward-hacking audit against the /analyst/grade oracle. benchmark/ is an agent-evaluation harness (run_benchmark.py, run_full_benchmark.py, ablation.py, backtesting.py, statistics.py, visualize.py) plus committed result artifacts in benchmark/results/ and 5 historical-crisis JSONs in benchmark/crisis_library/.
verdict: Split personality. The test suite is the single most genuinely engineered part of this audit scope: real behavioral assertions (smart strategy must beat do-nothing, seeds must jitter, cascades must inject, reward hacks must score low), determinism proofs, and receipts whose sha256 hashes actually verify. It even caught a real regression â€” 8 adversarial tests fail TODAY because server/app.py still points at the pre-reorg "v3_arcadia/results/R4_DANGEROUS_V2.json" path â€” but nobody noticed because CI is entirely disabled, and the "requires Ollama+GPU" excuse is false: the 176 passing tests are CPU-only with zero network calls (I ran them in 140s). The benchmark/ directory, by contrast, is substantially theater: run_benchmark.py silently substitutes the scripted baseline for all 8 "trained" agents, ablation.py inherits that so its committed ablation_results.csv has six rows ("+CVaR", "+DT", "+Ensemble"...) byte-identical to Scripted; visualize.py contains three fully fabricated hardcoded "publication-quality" figures (benchmark table, ablation bars, radar chart); backtesting.py's own committed output says is_credible=false on all 3 crises and compares 0 metrics for Red Sea due to a key-name mismatch; statistics.py crashes on a missing CSV whose generator was exiled to _dump; and the 5 crisis_library JSONs are dead data nothing loads.
